post.caption: The briolette has no flat top. Most cut gems have a flat facet on top called the table. A pear shape has a table, but a briolette has none. A briolette is covered all over with triangular facets. So it has no front or back and catches light everywhere. Drilled at the narrow end, it hangs freely from a wire. That is why briolettes are usually drop pendants and earrings. GIA researchers link the cut to India, by the 1600s. A French gem merchant sold briolettes to King Louis the Fourteenth. Napoleon's necklace for his empress includes briolettes and sits in the Smithsonian.
